title: Harmonize SDK transport layers and pin minor dependency versions across Python/JS/Go
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: Reduce long-term maintenance and runtime variance by aligning transport implementations and pinning compatible minor versions for SDK dependencies across Python, JS, and Go. This ticket covers dependency bumps that are non-breaking within semver minors (e.g., requests 2.31.x -> 2.32.x where appropriate), removal of deprecated API shims in client surfaces, and micro-refactors to remove duplicated transport logic that led to inconsistent retry / timeout behavior.

Scope:
- Audit current SDK dependencies and transitive versions for Python, JS, and Go.
- Pin minor versions in top-level package manifests and add a verification CI job that detects accidental float upgrades.
- Replace bespoke HTTP transport implementations with the shared transport helpers where safe (align header handling, timeouts, backoff).
- Remove deprecated client surface helpers flagged in previous audits and add migration helpers in CHANGELOGs.
- Ensure compatibility in streaming and chunked response handling (JS streaming + Python async iterators + Go readers).
- Add performance microbenchmarks to prevent regressions (token throughput and tail latency for small-batch sync and async paths).

Non-goals: major version upgrades with breaking API changes (those will be separate tickets), full rewrite of SDKs, expanding feature surface.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All three SDKs have pinned minor ranges added (or lockfiles updated) and CI guard job passing.
2) Transport behavior parity validated for retries/timeouts in a shared test matrix (unit + integration against local test harness).
3) Deprecated client helpers removed or replaced with documented aliases and migration notes in each SDK CHANGELOG.
4) PRs merged for python/js/go with green CI and no increased percent of flaky tests.
5) Release notes drafted and communicated to SDK consumers + engineering teams.

Risks & mitigations:
- Some environments rely on older transitive deps (e.g., enterprise customers pining older urllib3). Mitigation: provide opt-out docs and follow-on compatibility patch for Private customers.
- Streaming semantics subtly differ between runtimes. Mitigation: add e2e harness that replays representative payloads (LLM streaming tokens) during CI.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (spike): dependency audit + target minor ranges + CI job for version drift detection.
- Week 2: implement transport alignment in JS and Python (smaller surface area), open PRs and start reviews.
- Week 3: finish Go changes, run perf microbenchmarks, address regressions.
- Week 4: merge, cut patch releases for each SDK, update CHANGELOGs and notify customers.

Notes: this ticket ties into ongoing runtime work (ENG-19734) but focuses on client-side consistency and immediate maintenance debt.
